title: ÆON topic package manifest
description: The manifest.yaml at the root of a deep-dive library package (library/<id>/manifest.yaml). A package is curated epistemic scaffolding for one subject — where the good evidence is and how the subject hangs together — that seeds the research and mapping phases of a journey. It is an accelerator and MUST NOT limit ÆON Learn to predefined subjects (LIB-1): an agent behaves identically for a subject with no package. The manifest is the only required file of a package; the deeper curation lives in its sibling YAML files, which this schema does not govern.

id.title: Package identifier
id.description: The package's stable name, identical to its directory under library/. Other packages reference it in related_packages and prerequisites, so it is renamed only as a breaking change.

name.title: Package name
name.description: The subject as a person would name it, for catalogues and for the agent to echo back to the learner.

version.title: Package version
version.description: Bumped whenever the curation changes. It is how an agent judges how stale the curation may be before it researches on top of it — a package is a starting point that live research still checks, never a substitute for research.

domains.title: Knowledge domains
domains.description: The fields this subject spans. Each one becomes a research and mapping dimension, so a domain named here is a promise that the curation covers that literature.

canonical_sources.title: Canonical sources
canonical_sources.description: The works any serious treatment of the subject consults, as citation lines — enough for a reader to identify the work. This list is the manifest's summary, not the evidence map: tier classification, URLs, kinds and relevance belong in the package's canonical-sources.yaml, which is why entries here are plain text rather than records.
examples: F. A. Hayek: The Use of Knowledge in Society (1945)

learning_paths.title: Learning paths
learning_paths.description: The routes through the subject this package supports, named as slugs. They are offered to the curriculum compiler as shapes a journey can take; the compiler still sequences from the knowledge map and the discovered learner rather than serving a path verbatim.

prerequisites.title: Prerequisite packages
prerequisites.description: Packages a learner is better off having met first, by id. Empty is the normal case: a package that needs a prerequisite is usually a package whose own foundation section is missing.

description.title: Package description
description.description: What this package covers and why it exists as its own package, for a reader deciding whether it is the right accelerator.

epistemic_core.title: Epistemic core
epistemic_core.description: The one judgement about evidence that a teacher of this subject must hold — typically which of its claims are settled and which are routinely overstated. Packages whose literature spans several confidence levels carry it so the gradient is taught rather than flattened (EPI-5).

related_packages.title: Related packages
related_packages.description: Other library packages that neighbour this one, by id: the subjects it argues with, supplies primitives to, or is most often confused with. Used for the recommended next path at completion.

popular_lenses.title: Person lenses
popular_lenses.description: Public figures through whom many learners first meet this subject, so an invocation like "teach me what X teaches" can be accelerated by the underlying subject package while the person's own material is tiered honestly. A lens is framing, not authority.

$comment: The manifest stays open because a package is curation, and curation grows: the library README names related_packages and popular_lenses as established extras, and packages have since added description and epistemic_core. Everything the library documents has a place above, so agents converge on one spelling per concept; anything a curator adds beyond that is accepted rather than rejected by a schema that cannot have anticipated it.

examples.name: Austrian Economics
canonical_sources: Ludwig von Mises: Economic Calculation in the Socialist Commonwealth (1920)
F. A. Hayek: The Use of Knowledge in Society (1945)
Israel M. Kirzner: Competition and Entrepreneurship (1973)

nonEmptyString.description: Text that carries content. An empty string is a missing field wearing a disguise.

packageId.description: A library package id: lower-case ASCII words joined by single hyphens, so that it works unchanged as a directory name, a URL segment and a cross-reference. The repository is aeon-protocol and a package is austrian-economics, even where the prose keeps the ÆON ligature.

pathSlug.description: A learning-path name in the same slug form as a package id, so paths can be named on a command line, in a URL or in an invocation without quoting.

version.description: A monotonically increasing revision: a counter, or a dotted version string. Both forms exist in the library today.

sourceTier.description: The genre of a source on the four-point scale of RES-5: 1 primary source, 2 high-quality synthesis, 3 expert interpretation, 4 popular explanation. Tier records genre, not importance, and tiers are calibrated within a package — comparing tiers across packages is unsupported.

personLens.title: Person lens
personLens.description: One public figure learners arrive through, with the honest placement of their own material.

name.description: The person, named as they are publicly known.

role.description: Why learners arrive through this person: what they wrote, host or built that puts them between the learner and the subject.

tier.description: Where this person's own material sits on the source-tier scale — usually 4 for popular work, higher for peer-reviewed collaborations. It is the placement, not a verdict on the person.

note.description: What a teacher should know about using this lens: the gap between the popular presentation and the literature, and any named critique. No hagiography, no hit piece.
